a:r.a:t: Originally, I’m from Holstebro and went to school and high school in Holstebro. A lot of my family lives there today. In 2010 I moved to Aarhus. In fact, I started at Aarhus teacher training college, but after six months I found out that I didn’t want to teach kids and I wanted to do something with IT.
I have two kids, Alicia and Ida. Alicia is nearly six years old and Ida just turned three.
I like music, love to sing and play a little bit of piano. I’m a bit into photography. I also do a lot of sports, go to the gym, go for a run and play tennis in summer.
Want to tell you about my arm – it’s not going to be a distraction for you to learn or for me to teach.

My right arm is partly paralyzed and has been since birth. I was stuck on my way out and they had to pull me out. Then the broke some nerves and something in my shoulder so it hasn’t been able to grow that much since. It is no big deal and I prefer that you ask instead of pretending nothing is wrong. I’m totally cool about it.

You might image how much work my left hand needs to do and it’s hard to code every day. During my master I started to fell a lot of pain in my left arm. Instead of getting sad I thought of alternatives: Teacher
